rendered: The review starts from the known global cobalt reserves, taken from the USGS report on cobalt: 7 million metric tons[1]. It then applies a conservative yearly mining efficiency of ≈70%[2], and assumes that ≈40%[3] of the mined cobalt is directed toward battery manufacturing. Multiplying the reserves by the mining efficiency and by the battery share gives the cobalt usable for batteries. The paper's own recomputation states the result as ≈2 million metric tons[4] globally, which is the total usable battery-specific cobalt from the reserves. Without Co-free cathodes or recycling, cobalt demand is said to exceed the cobalt available for battery manufacturing before 2045[5].
